reference.title: Reference your rules {'|'} Public rules registry
reference.heading: Publish your rules, keep control of them
reference.lead: Your administration applies calculation rules. Referencing them in the registry makes them discoverable, traceable and reusable by other public services.
reference.processLead: Referencing starts with a minimal record, enriched afterwards according to what you can publish.
reference.step1Desc: Title, legal basis, rule owner, policy area. The minimum to make it discoverable.
reference.step2Desc: The articles, decrees or agreements it rests on, linked to their Légifrance source.
reference.step3Desc: From plain referencing to an executable model: each level brings its own value, at your own pace.
reference.step4Desc: Its record states what it offers - discovery, traceability, calculation - according to the evidence supplied.
reference.levelsTitle: How far you want to go
reference.levelsLead: A rule brings value as soon as it is referenced. Documenting it and then making it executable are optional steps, taken when you are ready.
reference.level1Title: The rule exists and can be found
reference.level1Body: Metadata and legal basis. The rule becomes discoverable in the registry and linked to its texts.
reference.level1Requirement: Open to any administration, with no technical prerequisite.
reference.level2Body: The business logic is described, possibly with test cases. The record gains traceability.
reference.level2Requirement: Requires formalising the rate schedule or the conditions, with an executable model left optional.
reference.level3Body: The model (Publicodes, OpenFisca, Catala or a proprietary engine) allows a calculation, exposed through an API or a simulator.
reference.level3Requirement: Assumes a calculation engine and a team to maintain it.
reference.ownershipTitle: What you keep, what the registry adds
reference.ownershipLead: The producing administration stays in charge of its rule; the registry exposes it.
reference.ownership1Body: The content of the rule, its accuracy and its publication belong to your administration. The registry reinterprets nothing.
reference.ownership2Body: You publish versions at your own pace, at every regulatory change. The history stays yours.
reference.ownership3Body: Discoverability, traceability up to the text and reuse by other services: this is what referencing adds.
reference.audiencesLead: Any administration or organisation that produces calculation rules binding on users can reference them.
reference.audience1Body: CNAF, DGFiP, France Travail… Reference the benefits and taxes you compute to make them traceable and reusable.
reference.audience2Body: Regions, departments, metropolitan areas, municipalities: your local schemes gain visibility and readability alongside national ones.
reference.audience3Body: Social security bodies and public operators: expose your rules once, instead of seeing them reinterpreted service by service.
reference.accompaniment: Referencing is supported by the team today: the registry team frames the scope, the legal basis and the intended publication level with you. A self-service administration area is being prototyped.
reference.ctaBody: Let us talk about referencing them: the registry team supports you, from the minimal record to the executable rule.

verify.title: Verify a rule {'|'} Public rules registry
verify.heading: From the displayed result up to the legal text
verify.lead: Every algorithmic decision has to be explainable. The registry links each calculation rule to the regulation it rests on, so that anyone can understand and check where an entitlement comes from.
verify.chainTitle: The chain that links the law to the calculation
verify.chainLead: Between the text that was voted and the amount displayed to the user, there are several translations. The registry makes each of them visible and verifiable.
verify.step1Desc: The article or the decree the rule rests on.
verify.step2Desc: The administrative interpretation: the rate schedule, the conditions.
verify.step3Desc: The executable model that computes the result.
verify.step4Desc: An amount or an eligibility, traceable up to its source.
verify.historyTitle: The state of the law, at a given date
verify.historyLead: Every regulatory change produces a new version, dated and linked to the text that triggered it. This tells which rule applied at a precise moment.
verify.timelineRule: Prest'Agri - family quotient and school allowance
verify.timelineProducer: · produced by the Ministry of Agriculture
verify.guarantee1Title: Every rule is linked to its text
verify.guarantee1Body: Act, decree, order, agreement or local decision: the legal basis of each rule is referenced and linked to its official source (Légifrance, ELI and LEGIARTI identifiers).
verify.guarantee2Body: At every change in the regulation, a new version of the rule is published. The state of the law applicable at a given date remains available.
verify.guarantee3Body: According to the evidence supplied by the rule owner (open code, test cases, certification), the rule gains a level of guarantee, stated clearly on its record.
verify.ctaTitle: See traceability on a real rule
verify.ctaBody: Open a record and explore the “Legal basis” tab: each rule exposes the texts it rests on and the history of its versions.

reuse.title: Reuse the rules {'|'} Public rules registry
reuse.heading: A rule modelled once, reused everywhere
reuse.lead: The registry exposes eligibility and calculation rules as common building blocks, ready to integrate and up to date with the law in force.
reuse.audiencesLead: Reusing an official rule brings reliability and compliance, while the calculation is written and maintained elsewhere.
reuse.audience1Body: Plug an eligibility or amount calculation directly into your online procedure, to inform the user at the right moment.
reuse.audience2Body: Rely on rules that are up to date and explainable to support a person and understand why an entitlement is granted or refused.
reuse.audience3Body: Consume the official rules at the source, or audit public policies from the code in force.
reuse.modesTitle: Three ways to integrate a rule
reuse.modesLead: The integration mode depends on the engine of the rule and on its publication level. Each record states precisely which ones are available.
reuse.mode1Body: For executable rules, a documented API returns a result from a described situation. Stable input and output contracts.
reuse.mode1Availability: Available as soon as a rule exposes a calculation engine (OpenFisca, Publicodes, Catala or an open proprietary engine).
reuse.mode2Body: A simulation module ready to embed (iframe or web component) on a website, with light development.
reuse.mode2Availability: Reserved for light engines executable in the browser (Publicodes, Catala).
reuse.mode3Body: For light engines, the rule can run client-side - suited to mobile use and respectful of privacy.
reuse.mode3Availability: Distributed as an npm package for the rules whose model is published.
reuse.modesNote: Some rules stay operated internally by the producing administration and are reusable only inside its own systems.
reuse.ctaBody: Open the record of an executable rule and read the “API” tab: endpoint, input format and response example are documented there.

apiService.title: Run a rule in the registry {'|'} Public rules registry
apiService.heading: A rule executed in the registry, an API in service
apiService.lead: The administration publishes the code of its rule and describes it in a manifest. The registry records it, runs it on demand and exposes a documented API, ready to integrate in a service.
apiService.tagExecutionHint: The registry hosts the code published by the administration and runs it at the recorded version.
apiService.tagLanguagesHint: One adapter per language loads the code and passes it the validated input.
apiService.tagAccessHint: Every call carries an access token in the Authorization header.
apiService.placesLead: Each record states where the calculation takes place and what the registry checks about it. Three cases exist today.
apiService.place1Body: The administration operates its own API. The registry documents the call, runs the test cases and dates every check.
apiService.place1Example: Prest'Agri, API of the Ministry of Agriculture
apiService.place2Body: The code of the rule is pinned to a version and executed in the browser or on the user's device, with its explanation.
apiService.place3Body: The administration publishes its code and a manifest. The registry runs it and exposes an API ready to call; the administration keeps its code, its versions and its responsibility.
apiService.stepsTitle: How a rule becomes an API
apiService.stepsLead: The code stays the administration's. The registry adds registration, input validation and execution.
apiService.step1Desc: A Python module, or a Catala program compiled to Python before publication. The generated module is what gets deployed.
apiService.step2Label: Describe the rule in a manifest
apiService.step2Desc: Identifier, language, entrypoint, input and output schemas, maximum duration, source files.
apiService.step3Desc: One HTTP call. The registry keeps the manifest under its identifier.
apiService.step4Desc: A situation in JSON. The registry validates the input, runs the code and returns the result with its provenance.
apiService.serviceTitle: The execution service, call by call
apiService.serviceLead: The example followed here is a family quotient written in Catala, compiled to Python and registered in the registry.
apiService.manifestLead: A JSON document, common to every language. The language and the entrypoint determine the adapter that runs the code; the schemas set the input and output contract.
apiService.manifestFieldId: Unique identifier in the registry, reused in the execution URL.
apiService.manifestFieldLanguage: “python” or “catala”: selects the adapter that runs the code.
apiService.manifestFieldEntrypoint: How to load and call the code: a type (“python:class”, “catala:scope”) and a “module:attribute” target.
apiService.manifestFieldInputSchema: JSON Schema of the input. Every call is validated against this schema before execution.
apiService.manifestFieldOutputSchema: JSON Schema of the returned result.
apiService.manifestFieldSource: Source files of the rule, for traceability.
apiService.manifestFieldSampleInputs: One example of a valid input, to test the registration.
apiService.registerLead: An authenticated call deposits the manifest. The registry keeps it under its identifier and the execution API opens at that address.
apiService.routeRegister: Registers a manifest, or replaces the one carrying the same identifier.
apiService.routeInferSchema: Generates the input and output schemas from a compiled Catala module.
apiService.routesToken: Every route requires an access token (header
apiService.executeLead: The situation is sent in JSON to the address of the rule. The registry validates it against the input schema of the manifest, then the adapter runs the code within the declared time limit.
apiService.outcomeSuccessText: Result computed, with its provenance: adapter, module and scope executed.
apiService.outcomeFailedText: The rule refused the calculation (missing value, division by zero, assertion). The message comes from the program itself.
apiService.outcomeErrorText: Technical incident in the adapter or the infrastructure.
apiService.outcomeRejectedText: The input contradicts the schema of the manifest. The code was not executed.
apiService.adaptersLeadAfter: designates the adapter. Each one validates the input, loads the code from the entrypoint, calls it and returns a response of the same shape.
apiService.adapterPythonBody: A function or a class importable by the service, called with the validated input and expected to return a JSON object matching the output schema.
apiService.adapterPythonDetail: A package following the regalgo convention (compute method, data + context input) registers as it is.
apiService.adapterCatalaBody: The Catala program is compiled to Python before publication. The adapter imports the generated module and calls the function of the scope.
apiService.adapterCatalaDetail: The JSON input is converted to the Catala types (money, integer, decimal, boolean, date, option, list, structure) and the output returned as JSON.
apiService.adaptersNote: For Catala, the input and output schemas are generated from the types of the compiled module, with one example input. An external type (an enumeration with a payload in the input) is handled by a short Python module, registered as a Python algorithm.
apiService.catalaTitle: The Catala example, from source to result
apiService.catalaLead: Same chain as Prest'Agri: the rule is written in Catala, compiled before publication, and the generated module is what runs.
apiService.catalaSourceNote: The household counts one share per child in addition to the agent's own; the household income is divided by that number of shares. For 32,000 € and two children, the quotient comes to 10,666.67 € over three shares.
apiService.chain1Desc: The text of the rule, readable by a lawyer, and its executable transcription.
apiService.chain2Desc: Done before publication, with the Catala toolchain.
apiService.chain3Desc: What gets deployed. It depends only on the Python standard library.
apiService.chain4Desc: The adapter imports the module and calls the function of the scope.
apiService.linkPrestagri: Prest'Agri, a Catala rule in production
apiService.linkSourceCode: Source code of the execution service
apiService.ctaTitle: Compare with an API operated by the rule owner
apiService.ctaBody: The Prest'Agri record documents the API of the Ministry of Agriculture: address, parameters, response example and dated checks.
